parameters.content:
## MP4 Download Path
- This path downloads the MP4 video file from SermonAudio and will hopefully clip and create YouTube Shorts.
- The first node gets the latest sermon from SermonAudio using an api call url.
- The next node extracts the MP4 url from that sermon data.
- The third node downloads the MP4 file.
- The final node, a set node, is present to retain the downloaded file as a specific variable and to maintain the sermon title.

nodes.name: Organization and clean-up of the transcript

parameters.content:
## MP3 Download
- The first node is a cron trigger, which is set to run every Sunday at 8 PM. This trigger applies right now specifically to my church's upload schedule.
- The next node uses an rss feed url to get the latest sermon from SermonAudio.
- The next node then parses that data from XML to JSON.
- The sermon data is then extracted, including the MP# url, before being passed to the next node.
- The final node in this highlighted portion downloads the MP3 and then passes that binary data on.

## Transcription
- I ended up using AssemblyAI for the actual transcription due to its ability to handle file sizes up to about 500 MB. Later I will implement OpenAI for cleanup and generative nodes.
- The first node in this section uploads the MP3 to AssemmblyAI.
- The next node then transcribes the sent MP# file.
- The third node provides a time period of about 60 seconds to avoid maxing out rate limits and allows the transcription just enough time to complete without wasting valuable seconds.
- The fourth node checks for transcription completion.
- The next node checks transcription status similar to the previous node, but if the status is not complete, the process gets sent back to the wait node to give the transcription process more time.
- The second-to-last node extracts important transcript data like the transcript text and the summaries.
- Finally, the OpenAI message node takes the generated transcript and organizes it into clear and concise paragrpahs and points.

## Blog Post/Social Media Caption Generations
- Basically, this section of the workflow is the generation and approval/denial/editing phase of the system.
- The first flow is the Blog Post generation. OpenAI analyzes the transcript using a prompt and spits out a suggested blog post. The following nodes are for approval/denial/editing/human-in-the-loop actions.
- The second flow is the social media caption generation. OpenAI again analyzes based on a prompt and spits out a result that is reviewed and approved/denied/edited/sent for review.

## Human-In-The_Loop 
- First node is for the emailing of the transcript to an editor for review. If approved it goes on the true path of the next node (IF node), if not it goes down the false path.
- The next node is already explained as a condition setter.

## Blog Post/Social Media Caption Generations
- Basically, this section of the workflow is the generation and approval/denial/editing phase of the system.
- The first flow is the Blog Post generation. OpenAI analyzes the transcript using a prompt and spits out a suggested blog post. The following nodes are for approval/denial/editing/human-in-the-loop actions.
- The second flow is the social media caption generation. OpenAI again analyzes based on a prompt and spits out a result that is reviewed and approved/denied/edited/sent for review.

## Transcript Editing
- This section literally just creates a google doc for the denied transcript, sends the editor an email, requests editing and review with a 2 hour time limit, and then sends the transcript along the path.
